title: Count the non-blank lines of a file and close what you open

blocks.text: `Files.lines(path)` reads a file lazily, line by line, but the stream it returns holds an open file handle. It is `AutoCloseable`, and it must be closed, which is what try-with-resources is for.

items: `countNonBlank(Stream<String> lines)` returns how many of the lines are not blank (blank as `String.isBlank()` means it: empty, or only whitespace, Unicode spaces such as U+2003 included), and **closes** the stream it was given before returning, even when counting fails with an exception.

`countNonBlank(Path file)` returns the same count for the lines of a UTF-8 text file, decoded as UTF-8. `Files.lines` reads it lazily; its stream should be closed too, although the tests can only watch the closing in method 1.

blocks.text: "Blank" is wider than "empty", and a stream you were handed to consume is yours to close.

cases.says: It counts the lines that are not blank, from a stream and from a file.
The stream of lines is closed when counting ends, as try-with-resources does; an unclosed Files.lines stream leaks a file handle.
A line of only whitespace is blank, as String.isBlank() sees it: spaces, tabs, and Unicode spaces such as U+2003, read from a UTF-8 file.
The stream is closed even when counting throws, as try-with-resources guarantees; a close() after the count is skipped by the exception.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A stream from Files.lines holds an open file and is closed with try-with-resources.
